To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the spectral brightness of an organic dye laser can be increased by a factor of 8.5 by using two coupled resonators and by electro-optically switching the Q factor of the laser during pumping.

(1) a laser with two coupled resonators and electronic switching of the coupling factor between them is a promising source of tunable radiation with high spectral brightness and efficiency; (2) the spectral brightness of this laser is 2.5 times higher and the efficiency is 8.5 higher than those of a laser with a single resonator.

The use of an electro-optic switch in a coupled resonator dye laser leads to a 9-fold increase in the spectral brightness of the output radiation, compared to a similar laser with one dispersive resonator.
